$comment: The GM tool contract. ONE copy, two languages: TypeScript imports it via @deliberate/protocol (GM_TOOLS) and the Python GM service loads it with deliberate_gm.contracts.load_tools. `tools` is one flat array in the order the model sees it — queries first, then mutations — and that order must stay stable because the tool list is the head of the cached prompt prefix. Each entry carries `kind`: "query" means free and read-only (it never touches the world and never consumes the seeded RNG), "mutation" means it maps onto exactly one engine Intent and is validated before anything changes. `kind` lives here rather than as a hardcoded name list in each language, so adding a tool is a one-file change; loaders drop it when building the Anthropic `tools` parameter, which takes only name, description and input_schema. Every input_schema sets additionalProperties:false and lists every property in `required` (optional arguments are nullable rather than absent) because the service calls the model with strict schemas. Decision 2 of docs/m1-swarm.md.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Read the authoritative world state. Free and read-only: it never changes anything and never consumes a die roll. Use it before deciding anything; never guess at positions, hit points or whose turn it is.

scope.description: world: flags, quests and the clock. entities: every creature with its components. initiative: turn order and the current turn's economy. map: the tile grid as ASCII rows, who stands where, and this location's exits, frontiers and objectives — a frontier is an edge of the world nothing has been written beyond. all: everything (large; prefer a narrower scope).

entity_id.description: With scope 'entities', return only this entity. Null for all of them; ignored by the other scopes.

tools.name: legal_actions
tools.description: Everything this entity may legally do right now, computed by the engine's own validators: how far it may still move and to which tiles, which targets it can attack or cast at with which weapon or spell, and whether it may end its turn. Rejected options come back with the reason the engine would give. Free and read-only.

entity_id.description: The entity whose options to enumerate.

tools.name: line_of_sight
tools.description: Whether a straight line from tile a to tile b is unobstructed, plus the distance between them. Free and read-only.

a.description: Origin tile. Integer grid coordinates; x runs east, y runs south.

map.description: Map id. Null picks the only loaded map, and errors if more than one is loaded.

tools.name: path
tools.description: Shortest 8-way walking route from tile a to tile b costing at most max_cost tiles, avoiding walls, steep steps and occupied squares. One tile is 5 ft. Free and read-only.

max_cost.description: Budget in tiles; each step, diagonal or not, costs one.

map.description: Map id. Null picks the only loaded map.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Search the world record for what is already established about a topic: world flags, quests and their current step, entities and their dialogue seeds. This is the engine's memory of facts, not your narrative memory. Free and read-only.

topic.description: Case-insensitive substring to look for in flag keys, quest ids, titles and steps, entity ids and names.

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return, in a stable order.

tools.name: roll_preview
tools.description: The odds of a prospective attack or spell attack: the attack bonus, the target's AC, whether advantage or disadvantage applies and why, the chance to hit, the chance to crit, and the expected damage. Computed analytically from the rules — it does NOT roll and does NOT consume the seeded RNG, so calling it never changes what the real roll will be. Free and read-only. If the action would be illegal you get the engine's rejection reason instead of odds.

kind.description: attack: a weapon attack. cast: a spell attack.

ability.description: Weapon key for kind 'attack' (e.g. longsword), spell key for kind 'cast' (e.g. fire_bolt).

tools.name: move
tools.description: Walk an entity to a tile. The engine validates the route, the movement budget and the turn order, and rejects anything illegal without changing the world. Maps to the same validated `move` intent the player's UI sends.

tools.name: attack
tools.description: Make a weapon attack. The engine rolls it from the seeded RNG, applies damage and spends the action (or the bonus action for an off-hand light weapon). The first attack starts an encounter and rolls initiative. Maps to the validated `attack` intent.

ability.description: Weapon key from the trimmed SRD table: unarmed, club, dagger, handaxe, mace, shortsword, longsword, greataxe, shortbow, longbow. The attacker must carry it unless it is natural.

tools.name: cast
tools.description: Cast an attack cantrip at a target. Resolves through the same validated attack pipeline as a weapon: range, line of sight, action economy, a seeded attack roll and damage. Maps to the validated `cast` intent.

spell.description: Spell key from the trimmed cantrip table: fire_bolt, ray_of_frost, eldritch_blast.

tools.name: say
tools.description: Have an entity speak. This is the one mutation that changes no world state: it emits a dialogue line for the player to read and leaves the state hash untouched. The engine still validates it, so a dead or unknown speaker is rejected.

text.description: What they say, in their own voice.

to.description: Who they address. Null for speaking to the room.

tools.name: set_disposition
tools.description: Move how one entity feels about another by a delta. The engine clamps the result to [-100, 100] and records your reason. Maps to the validated `set_disposition` intent.

toward.description: Who they are feeling it about.

delta.description: Change to apply. Positive is warmer; the result is clamped to [-100, 100].

reason.description: Why it changed, in one short phrase. Recorded with the diff.

tools.name: spawn
tools.description: Place a new creature from a known template onto a tile. The engine rejects unknown templates, blocked or occupied tiles and duplicate ids; if an encounter is running the newcomer rolls initiative and is spliced into the order without changing whose turn it is. Maps to the validated `spawn` intent.

template_id.description: Key of a template the engine was configured with. Unknown templates are rejected; the reply lists the known ones.

at.description: Tile to place the creature on. Must be on the map, walkable and empty.

map.description: Map id. Null picks the only loaded map.

entity_id.description: Id for the new entity. Null derives a unique one from the template id.

tools.name: set_flag
tools.description: Set a world flag: the durable record that something happened. Maps to the validated `set_flag` intent.

key.description: Flag name. Reuse an existing key rather than inventing a synonym; call recall first.

tools.name: advance_quest
tools.description: Move a quest to a later step. The engine rejects unknown quests, steps out of range and any step that is not strictly forward of the current one. Maps to the validated `advance_quest` intent.

step.description: Index into the quest's steps. Must be greater than the current step and within range.

tools.name: end_turn
tools.description: End the acting entity's turn and pass initiative on, skipping the dead and anyone with no brain that can act. Maps to the validated `end_turn` intent.

tools.name: author_map
tools.description: Write a location that did not exist: TERRAIN ONLY (`spawn` puts anyone in it). Call it when the player reaches a frontier — an exit whose `to` is null. `terrain` uses the alphabet `get_state` gives you: `#` wall, `.` floor, `1`-`9` raised that high, a step climbing at most 1. Tiles are `[x, y]`. Every way out and objective must be walkable-reachable from the entrance, and no floor may be walled off from it, or the engine refuses the map and says why. A refusal changes nothing: fix what it names and call again.

map_id.description: Id for the new location, e.g. "north-road". Must be free.

back.description: The way in. `at` is this map’s entrance; `to` is a loaded map with a frontier at `arrive`.

at.description: [x, y] here you arrive on. Must be floor.

label.description: How the way back looks from here.

at.description: [x, y] of the edge tile. Floor, and reachable.

frontiers.description: New undefined edges for a later call. May be empty.

objectives.description: Why the place is worth walking into. May be empty.

at.description: [x, y] it sits on. Floor, and reachable.

note.description: One line you can act on later.

quest.description: An existing quest id, or null.
